# lane <TAB> setup
# These were the `*` rows in suites.tsv, and they were never suites: a window
# manager, a toolkit, a default leash and the toolkit a lane draws with are
# facts about the machine, not about anything it runs. With one row per suite
# next door there is nowhere for them to sit, and that is the right pressure --
# they are a different table because they are a different thing.
# Every suite row on a lane merges over its lane row, left to right, so what is
# left in a suite row is only what makes that row different. A suite saying
# `display=off` overrides a lane saying `display=metacity` by plain assignment.
# `<lane>:<phase>` names one pass of a lane that runs its list more than once:
# linux-engines swaps its engine packages between halves. Everything left of the
# colon is what reaches $NT_LANE, so cases.tsv and the grid never see a phase.
# `toolkit=` is the one that was argv until now. Ten command columns passed
# `gtk`, `qt` or `macos` as a word, next to a setup column that already said
# `gtk` or `qt` for the display -- two spellings of one fact.
# `shots=` on a phase is where that phase's pictures go, and it is the reason
# the cjs half of linux-engines no longer needs a step to move its frames out
# of the way of the pygobject half's: the two halves never shared a directory
# to begin with, they only shared a default.
# windows-launch and macos-netinstall are here with no display and no toolkit
# because the one row each runs -- netinstall -- draws with neither. The other
# windows lane, wayland, bsd and kde-live have no row anywhere, and suites.tsv
# says why for each.
